findings.title: Concurrent observer writers bypass the advertised cumulative event and byte limits
findings.requirement: Section 4 requires an explicit cumulative event/byte bound in the same observer; monitoring explicitly covers new native threads.
findings.mechanism: emit checks shared counters, performs os.write, then updates the counters without serialization. os.write can release the GIL. Two threads can both pass the same last-slot check and both successfully write; the decoder's later truncation is fail/incomplete but does not enforce the producer's resource bounds.

source_reproducer.command: env -u PYTHONPATH -u PYTHONHOME -u MYPYPATH -u PYTEST_ADDOPTS -u PYTEST_PLUGINS PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 api/.venv/bin/python -I -B /home/kali/.hermes/cache/scratch/d01-d03-safety-4ea079c6/source-probe.py
source_reproducer.boundary: Exact BOOTSTRAP emitter extracted with ast/literal parsing; counters seeded to an admissible near-limit state; two threads paused after the check at a Barrier write seam, then the original bytes are actually written to an owned os.pipe. No Hermes or PostgreSQL import/launch.
source_reproducer.control: At identical counters and with identical 442-byte record, serial first write accepted and second write refused: events=256, bytes=65442.

findings.impact: The required producer bounds are not true on the supported threaded channel. This is not a demonstrated forbidden-body entry, private-data leak, native cause, or product effect.
findings.minimal_remedy: Serialize the emitter's limit check, complete write, and counter update with a suitable reentrancy-safe mechanism; retain record-before-denial and failure-on-unavailable behavior. Add one bounded concurrent last-slot regression on this same emitter, retaining the serial control and zero forbidden-body assertions. No broad harness or native retry is needed to close this SOURCE finding.
